public.privacy.data_text: Data may include client identifiers, age, sex, weight, session notes, sleep and recovery context, heart rate, HRV, SpO2, pulse, device metadata, timestamps, signal-quality information and check-in/session/recovery responses.
public.privacy.intro: CoreLabTech processes client profile information, session check-ins, uploaded physiology timelines, calculated wellness metrics and generated reports for the purpose of delivering wellness session insights.
public.privacy.notice_text: CoreLabTech provides wellness and educational insights. It is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent disease. This template should be reviewed for the provider's jurisdiction and business model before launch.
public.privacy.processor_text: For business customers, the wellness provider will normally determine the purposes of client-data processing and CoreLabTech will process data under the documented service and data-processing agreement. The final allocation of roles must be confirmed for each deployment.
public.privacy.purpose_text: Data is used to operate sessions, synchronize compatible files, calculate personal trends and generate client reports. Access should be limited to authorized staff of the wellness provider and the client where applicable.
public.privacy.retention_text: The wellness provider defines and documents the applicable retention period. Authorized staff can export a client's records in a portable archive and submit a controlled deletion. Exports and deletions are recorded in the operational audit log. Data should not be retained longer than required for the agreed wellness service or an applicable legal duty.
public.privacy.title: Privacy Notice

public.terms.accountability_text: Administrative actions, client exports, completed sessions and deletion requests may be recorded in an audit log. Retention periods and access rights are configured under the provider's approved data-governance policy.
public.terms.chamber_text: Operators must select the correct chamber, wellness protocol and pressure unit. Trends for different target pressures, such as 1.3 and 1.5 ATA, are kept separate. The platform does not control the chamber and does not replace the manufacturer's operating instructions.
public.terms.data_quality_text: Operators should verify the selected client, device placement, file timestamps and synchronization quality. Missing HRV, low match rate or sensor disagreement reduces interpretation confidence.
public.terms.no_diagnosis_text: Scores, trends and reports are not diagnoses, treatment recommendations, medical clearance or emergency monitoring. A wellness result must not replace professional medical assessment where it is required.
public.terms.operator_text: The wellness provider remains responsible for session operation, informed client acknowledgement, staff permissions, data retention and appropriate escalation when a client reports discomfort or requests medical advice.
public.terms.scope_text: CoreLabTech supports documentation and interpretation of wellness sessions. Results are educational indicators derived from available sensor data, client context and configured rule-based calculations.
public.terms.title: Wellness Terms
public.wellness.intro: Use the same client, sensor setup and timing approach across repeat sessions. Consistency improves synchronization quality and makes the personal baseline more useful.

public.wellness.step6_text: Use 5 sessions for an early trend and 14 quality sessions for a stronger baseline.
